newsitem.title: MEXICO: Serfin Q2 seen stable, which is good news.
newsitem.headline: Serfin Q2 seen stable, which is good news.

text.p: Second quarter results for Grupo Financiero Serfin are expected to show similar profits and net interest margins to the first quarter, analysts said.
"Such is Serfin. Stable is good news. We don't expect anything spectacular," said Carlos Gomez, bank analyst at Paribas Capital Markets.

Most analysts declined to give precise estimates of its Q2 results, because the banking group has still more than $400 million outstanding of a capitalization commitment that needs to be completed before year end.

Merrill Lynch, however, said it could report a quarterly profit of one centavo per share, or one U.S. cent per American Depositary Share -- little change from the previous three-month period when its net profit was 46 million pesos.
The report is expected to be issued on July 21-22.
Analysts said its net interest margin could rise slightly from the 3.2 percent reported in the first quarter that the bank had said was close to break-even point.
Its past-due loan portfolio as a percentage of total loans was expected to remain close to the 22.6 percent it reported up to February. Significant loan growth was not expected.
"I don't see growth in total loans until the fourth quarter," said Robert Lacoursiere, analyst at Santander Investment.

In March, Serfin agreed in principal to sell a 19.9 percent stake to HSBC Holdings PLC for $300 million. In early July, Lincoln National Corp said it agreed to buy 49 percent of Serfin's insurance unit Seguros Serfin for $85 million. The deal was expected to close in the third quarter.
Both sales were aimed at boosting Banca Serfin's capital.
